title: recordsAt: a per-file ENOENT must not empty the whole directory snapshot (DEC-282 (a19) item 2)
description: DEC-282 (a19) item 2, option A (opum-doc ruling, relayed by the leader): fix the per-file ENOENT hazard in recordsAt for the NEXT pair release; no 0.15.2. Hazard (found while diagnosing QCLI-582, unmeasured as the cause of that failure): recordsAt in src/application/tasks/local-task-repository.ts (:286-306 at v0.15.1) lists a directory with readdir, then readFile per .json inside one Promise.all, and its catch turns ANY ENOENT (:302-304) into an empty list for the WHOLE directory. One listed file removed between readdir and readFile therefore makes every record in that directory read as absent, and findTask then throws task_not_found. A whole-directory ENOENT (the directory itself is missing) correctly returns an empty list and must keep doing so. Open design choice for the implementer, to be justified in the notes: skip only the vanished file, or retry the snapshot once. Scope note: line 280 has a similar ENOENT return; check whether it is the same hazard before touching it. Do not implement until dispatch-floor and the leader GO.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A readFile ENOENT on one listed record file no longer empties the directory: either only that file is skipped, or the snapshot is retried once; the choice is stated and justified in the task notes
A readdir ENOENT (the directory itself absent) still returns an empty list, as before
A test removes one .json between readdir and readFile and passes with the fix, and the same test fails against the pre-fix recordsAt
bun run check exits 0 on the pinned bun

implementationNotes: DESIGN CHOICE: retry the snapshot once, and skip a file that vanishes again. In recordsAt a readFile ENOENT on one listed record file now skips that file and reports it (onVanished) instead of emptying the whole directory; snapshot() repeats the whole five-directory scan once when anything vanished, and a file that vanishes again on the repeat is skipped for good. Why not skip-only: a record moved between directories by a lifecycle write (written to completed/, then removed from tasks/) can be missed in BOTH directories by a single unlocked pass, because the five directories are read concurrently and independently; skipping alone would then still report the record absent. A repeat re-reads every directory and finds it in the new one. Cost: nothing on the normal path (the repeat runs only when a file vanished; CountingRepository scan-count tests unchanged). The repeat never throws and never empties a directory. readdir ENOENT (directory absent) still returns an empty list; any non-ENOENT read error still propagates. A protected readRecordFile(path) seam was added so a test can simulate the vanish without mocking fs. LINE 280 (recoverLifecycle): checked, NOT the same hazard and left untouched. It reads one specific journal file, .lifecycle.journal.json; ENOENT there means no journal exists, so returning is the correct no-op, and it never converts a record read into an empty collection. CONTROL (red runs, test/qcli583-records-at-vanished-file.test.ts, 5 tests, all pass with the fix): against the pre-fix recordsAt (git show HEAD version) 4 of 5 fail (the sibling-survives test fails because T-1 and T-3 are missing: whole directory emptied; the other three fail because the readRecordFile seam does not exist pre-fix, so those are not clean behavioural controls). So two mutants of the FIXED code were run: M1 (per-file ENOENT throws into an outer catch that returns [], i.e. the old behaviour) turns exactly the sibling test and the retry test red (2 fail, 3 pass); M2 (the repeat scan removed) turns exactly the retry test red (1 fail, 4 pass). The unmutated fix passes all 5. CHECKS: with the pinned bun 1.4.2 (darwin-aarch64 zip, sha256 90987a3a16d7db556d886ac3d551e7b6d3edf0a1cf43acaed622e8676be1d12f, matching the published SHASUMS256.txt, PATH-prefixed) bun run check passed typecheck, lint (pre-existing warnings), format:check, layer:check and the full test arm (1553 pass, 0 fail, 163 files, including the 5 new tests), then exited 1 at the last arm test:mod: its typecheck reports TS errors in hooks/register.tsx that are not in a file this change touches (the known local mod-test-typecheck arm; CI reports NOT TYPECHECKED there). So bun run check did NOT exit 0 locally on its own; AC4 is left unchecked until the PR checks are green. Acceptance criteria stay unchecked until the independent review and landing.
